text:
**Short answer:** For most people, either is a solid free UK bank account. I’d lean **Starling as an everyday main account**, especially if you travel, use cash, or want a straightforward no-fee account. Choose **Monzo** if its budgeting tools and app experience suit you better.

| What matters | Monzo | Starling |
|---|---|---|
| **Monthly fee** | Free account; paid plans add extras | Free |
| **Travel spending** | No fee on card purchases abroad; ATM withdrawal limits depend on your account and circumstances | No fees from Starling for card spending or cash withdrawals abroad |
| **Cash deposits** | Usually a fee at PayPoint | Post Office deposits are free up to an annual limit |
| **Budgeting** | Strong budgeting and spending tools; paid plans add features | Spaces, spending insights and bill management |
| **Overdraft** | Rate depends on your offer; check the app | Rate depends on your offer too—don’t assume a headline rate applies to you |
| **Support** | App-based support | App-based support |

**My rule of thumb:**
- **Starling** for a simple main account, frequent travel, or occasional cash deposits.
- **Monzo** if you want its budgeting features, spending controls, or paid-plan extras.

Both are app-based rather than branch banks, so consider keeping a second account elsewhere if branch services matter. Also compare the current account terms directly before deciding: fees, withdrawal allowances, savings rates and overdraft offers can change, and overdrafts are personal.
